title: MOXIR beta v0.9, the epic plot, phase 1: where every device goes (placement options, measured)
status: PROPOSAL, sketches and numbers only, nothing built. Phase 1 of the epic plot: placement. The owner picks one option per group; phase 2 (looks, cues, fixture schedule, crew sheet, the rig file moxir-epic-2026-10-08.json) builds on his picks. Drawn and measured by scripts/place/epic_placement.py on top of rigs/moxir-lasers-v2-2026-10-08.json (lasers) and rigs/moxir-design-paint-2026-10-08.json (everything else).
owner: 2026-10-08: 'I want the EPIC placement: we have 6 LaserCubes, beams, wash and all info. Make the epic one please.'
2026-10-08 (order changed): 'yes go, but let's start from the PLACEMENT: give advice and sketches for the re-placement.'

fixed.what: the stage line z 24.5, the DJ centred on a 0.4 m step, PA at x +-5.4
the cut (12 m Prolyte H30V): NOT flipped, LOW 3.24 m house left, HIGH 6.35 m house right, hung from the near crane at z 21 behind the DJ, slid 1 m house left
the audience z 25.8-48 (x +-5.35 used); hall v8-show; the whole building (4 spans, far crane z -22.2)

no moving head on the truss; statics on the truss; no laser on the truss

laser_model.visibility_variant_why: the brief: treat the cubes as the 6 W unit (2700 / 1500 / 1800 mW) for what the floor sees, the conservative case
laser_model.safety_variant_why: the brief: the 10 W unit (5000 / 2800 / 2800 mW, NOHD 724 m) for every safety figure until a cube's label is read
laser_model.duty_why: a cube drawing 2 static beams is a 2-point scan: the galvos move the one beam between the two points, so each beam is on for at most half the time, less the blanked moves between them (blanking 10 % ASSUMED: not in the datasheet). The eye integrates a beam scanned far above flicker fusion to its time average (the Talbot-Plateau law), so the brightness seen per beam is 0.45 x the colour's power. The NOHD does NOT drop: IEC TR 60825-3 asks the show to plan for a scan failure, when the whole power stays in one beam.

options.title: goal-post truss at z -41.5 (his lean)
options.shows: 6 beams from 64 m behind the DJ, rising 1-2 m over 60 m: lines converging on the stage, the far half of the hall as the depth
options.rigging: a 12 m Prolyte H30V span (4 x L300) on two towers with base plates and outriggers; cubes on half-couplers + safeties under the bottom chord at 6.6 m
options.safety: cube 3 moves 2.5 m house left (x 7.3) or its beams hit the far crane's cab; tower stability check owed (ANSI E1.21 class)

options.title: the far crane rolled to z -41
options.shows: the most beam the floor sees (the trio sits clear of the far crane, because it IS the far crane)
options.rigging: girder clamps + 0.5 m drop arms on the far crane's front girder; the venue rolls the crane
options.safety: the crane locked out after the move (its operator, the venue's OK); no file says how far it can travel
options.cost: no truss rental; the venue's crane operator for the move and back

options.title: 'far, far away': towers at z -51.5
options.shows: the longest lines (about 73 m), but the floor sees the least of them: the far crane and the goal post's own span hide more
options.rigging: the same goal post 2.3 m in front of the far end wall
options.safety: as b; the sources sit about 90 m from the dance floor, deep in the haze the far half does not have yet

groups.why: Keep the goal post. With the honest power model (6 W, each cube's power split between its 2 beams) all three homes pass 6 of 6 and stay thousands of times above a dark club: a 299, b 227, c 149 cd/m2 per beam, seen on 74 / 65 / 54 % of their length. a is the brightest but needs the venue to roll a crane whose travel no file states; c is both dimmer (longer path through haze) and more hidden. 'Epic' does not argue for c: for the floor the lines are not longer, they are hidden more. b is his lean, the venue moves nothing.

groups.why: Feet and runway light about the same length of column (3.7 m vs 3.9 m), but the feet light the top half and the flared head, which is what reads from the floor as the hall's bones, and need no lift, no clamp and no crane lock-out. 3.5 m lights only the last metre. 2 of the 8 far nave units clip X bracing with a lens edge (1 % of their rays): slide them 0.3 m on the day. With the PAR's optional 25 deg lens the band would start lower, about 2 m (geometry, not run).

groups.title: Strobes and blinders (6 EXT-STROBE + 8 EXT-BLINDER, other supplier, 'full' version list)

options.title: on the truss's front face, aimed at the crowd
options.shows: the classic peak: the whole floor whited out (every eye in a field, about 40 000 lux at the front row with all 14 at once)
options.rigging: 14 units on the cut: 130 kg with clamps, 266 kg with its 17 PARs = 22 kg/m on a truss rated 321.6 kg/m (6 m span)
options.safety: eyes in the cones by design; strobes at most 4 flashes per second and a notice at the door (HSE, The Event Safety Guide HSG195)

options.title: behind the DJ, aimed up and back (floor strip behind the truss)
options.shows: the flash lights the haze and the steel behind the DJ: a white silhouette at the drop, the building flashing, no eye in a cone
options.rigging: floor, between the truss and the crane's back girder
options.safety: no eye in a cone; the 4 Hz rule still applies to the room

options.title: under the near crane's front girder (7.7 m), aimed steeply down onto the floor's front
options.shows: the crowd lit from above in the flash (every eye in a field, about 23 000 lux at the front row with all 14), the DJ dark
options.rigging: 14 girder clamps at 7.7 m (a lift); on the crane that is the beam stop and the truss's carrier
options.safety: eyes looking up are in the cones; adds load to the crane whose rating is owed

groups.why: Ash: the flash is the fire behind the DJ, not light in the crowd's eyes. 'behind' keeps every eye out of every field (front row 0 lux), puts no weight on the truss or the crane, and lights the near crane's steel and the machines behind the stage. Facing the crowd ('front', 'crane') is a show choosing glare at the peak: about 40 000 / 23 000 lux at the front row is a white-out; if he wants that hit, it is a choice made knowingly, at reduced intensity.

strobe_cd.basis: EQUIVALENT: Martin Atomic 3000 LED 180 000 lm (fixtures.json strobe.photometry) spread uniformly over a 60 deg cone (the angle ASSUMED there): I = flux / (2 pi (1 - cos 30 deg))

blinder_cd.basis: EQUIVALENT: Chauvet STRIKE 4, 999 lux at 5 m (fixtures.json blinder.photometry): I = E d^2

haze_model.reach_basis: ASSUMED: a hazer feeds the air within about 15 m of it (horizontal) in a still hall; no maker states a coverage. To measure on site with one unit running for 20 min, a beam swept along the nave (owed).
haze_model.volume_basis: nave 24 m x 107.6 m x 13 m to the deck (hall.json); the 4 spans 96.8 m x 107.6 m x 13 m
